- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon, especially after price spikes; apply downward bias of 2–5% for days 1–7.
- After a sharp price increase, model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.0), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for the first 5 days of forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in late forecast period (days 15–30); reduce forecast by 0.5–2% per day after day 15 if no new sentiment signal.
- Model ignores sentiment momentum; if sentiment rises >0.2 for 3+ consecutive days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
